elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered (h): "Customer may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate..." — the no-consent affiliate carve-out is retained and is now Customer-only.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered (h): "...or purchaser of all or substantially all of Customer's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction" without approval or consent. Covers merger/acquisition/asset-sale successors.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The general bar survives — "Neither Party may assign ... without the other Party's prior written consent" — and the proviso now runs only to Customer, so every Kubient assignment (affiliate, asset purchaser or merger successor included) requires Customer consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained verbatim: "prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld", applying to the consent Kubient must obtain from Customer.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative bar: "and Kubient may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Customer" — unconditional prohibition, reinforced by the retained "Any attempted assignment other than in accordance herewith will be void."

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no change-of-control or deemed-assignment trigger exists in the Agreement. Termination rights in 4(a)/(b) are limited to post-Initial-Term convenience on 90 days' notice, uncured material breach, and insolvency — none keyed to Customer's change of control, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the edit only Customer has the no-consent successor route; Kubient's successor/asset-purchaser assignments now require Customer's prior written consent, so the mutual successor right required by the fallback is absent.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered (h) contains no notice obligation for a permitted successor or affiliate assignment; the drafter did not add one.

A no-consent non-successor exception is retained for Customer ("without approval or consent to any affiliate"), which under the fallback test defeats the requirement that all non-successor assignments be consented to.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "which shall not be unreasonably withheld" is retained and governs every consent-required assignment by either Party.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the two Customer carve-outs and the reasonableness standard were already present, the edit converts the mutual no-consent exception to Customer-only (curing the Vendor free-assignment gap) and adds an express bar on assignment to a Customer competitor; no change-of-control trigger exists anywhere in the Agreement, so no deletion is needed for the last element.

Fallback is not met (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, and Customer's retained affiliate exception is a no-consent non-successor exception), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is satisfied.

Minimality holds: the only textual changes are "either Party"→"Customer", "said Party's"→"Customer's", and the inserted competitor bar — each tied to preferred elements 3 and 5. The void-assignment sentence, successors-and-assigns sentence, and entire-agreement sentences are retained verbatim; no survival tail, notice procedure, deemed-assignment definition, or other extras were added.

Intent is preserved: the amendment operates by narrowing an existing Vendor-side exception rather than granting Vendor any new assignment right; consent standard, void-assignment remedy, binding-effect language and all termination/fee mechanics in paragraph 4 survive without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

"Deviation" is the correct finding status for the original clause: as drafted, Kubient could assign to any affiliate, asset purchaser or merger successor without Customer consent and to a competitor, failing preferred elements 3 and 5 and also failing the fallback on the mutual no-consent exception.
